name: 606 panel
pending: Steps are written while the pattern runs, and stopped the step keys choose patterns, as the manual reads. That was not checked on a machine.

FUNCTION and CLEAR stay down once pressed, because a pointer cannot hold one key and press another: press FUNCTION, then a step key to make it the last step; press CLEAR, then the step key of the pattern to clear. On the machine they are held. A second press, or Esc, lets them up.

Two step keys are pressed together on the machine to chain patterns. Here: hold one and touch the other, press one and let go over the other, or hold Shift for the second. A chain is chosen while the machine is stopped; running, a step key chooses one pattern, which takes over at the bar line.

A track remembers the number of each bar's pattern, 1 to 16, and plays them in the group the PATTERN GROUP button stands on, because the engine has one switch for a whole song. Whether a bar keeps its own group on the machine is unverified.
Every track holds 64 bars. On the machine the last track holds more, and whether a full track runs on into the next is unverified; here it does not.

The segno bar (D.S.), choosing a bar by its number and STEP RESET are left out, so their lettering is not on the drawing. A bar is reached with BAR RESET and WRITE/NEXT, which leaves a bar as it was unless another pattern is chosen for it. A track always plays from its first bar and goes round, so CLEAR has nothing to reset in track play.
How the machine shows a bar's number is unverified. Here, with FUNCTION down in track write, the lamp of its tens is steady and the lamp of its units flashes, read against the BAR lettering.
PATTERN CLEAR leaves a pattern at sixteen steps and keeps its scale. What the machine does to the scale is unverified.

Turning the selector to an instrument plays it, and so does TAP while the machine is stopped in pattern write; the machine makes no sound for either. Turning the mode selector into or out of a track mode stops the machine here.
The volume knob clicks the power off at its left end, as on the machine. Pressing the POWER SW lettering beside it does the same, for anyone who cannot drag a knob.

The sockets lettered along the top edge are on the back of the machine: a pedal, sync, two trigger outputs, headphones, the output and power. This one has none of them, and one output with no stereo field.

The seven sounds are a model made from descriptions of the circuits. Nobody has listened to them yet, and nothing was measured from a machine. How far the level, accent and volume knobs reach is a guess, and the tempo knob runs from 40 to 300 beats a minute because that is the engine's range.
The lamps follow the manual where it describes them. What the hardware shows in the cases the manual leaves out is unverified.
